sanskrit_verse: उपास्य पश्चिमां संध्यां हुत्वाग्नींस्तान् उपास्य च / भृत्यैः परिवृतो भुक्त्वा नातितृप्त्याथ संविशेत् //
transliteration: upāsya paścimāṃ saṃdhyāṃ hutvāgnīṃs tān upāsya ca / bhṛtyaiḥ parivṛto bhuktvā nātitṛptyātha saṃviśet //
sph_interpretive_translation: Having worshipped the western Sandhyā and offered oblations into the fires, having again performed worship thereof, surrounded by servants, having eaten without excess, one should then sit composed.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority through disciplined ritual action establishes lawful presence
Causation arises from sequential sacred observances
Capacity-based responsibility requires regulation of bodily intake and mental composure
Restoration logic demands integration of service, consumption, and stillness
Consciousness alignment occurs through ordered devotional acts
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent performs Sandhyā worship AND offers oblations THEN agent fulfills preliminary dharma-duty
IF agent consumes food with servants present AND avoids satiation THEN agent maintains social dharmic posture
IF agent concludes activity sequence with seated composure THEN agent completes causal cycle
IF any step omitted THEN legal status remains ungrounded until completion
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating matters involving personal or institutional conduct, the Court must recognize that lawful presence and authoritative standing arise only when prescribed ritual and ethical sequences are fully executed. Omission or improvisation invalidates claim to jurisdiction or legitimacy.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that each act—worship, offering, eating, sitting—is a necessary link in the chain of lawful being. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures that skipping any stage disrupts alignment. Responsibility is proportional to capacity to perform all steps. Non-punitive reality holds that misalignment results not in penalty but in dissolution of legal standing.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Re-perform omitted ritual actions under supervision
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Public reaffirmation of sequential duties
Capacity Restoration: Training regimen for proper conduct of Sandhyā and offerings
Integrity Reintegration: Witnessed repetition of full sequence to restore lawful presence
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This law restores rightful order through conscious completion. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
